observations: ServicesAPI.RESOURCES.RESOLVE documents full dependency closure, but ResourceSet carries dependency-ordered group arrays and results, not edge records or snapshot-completeness proof.

ResourcesProvider.resolve calls addDependencies. Inspected addDependencies identifies namespace/model/definition roots and invokes addNamespacesToResultSet; behavior/component/project/resource dependencies remain comment-only follow-up categories.

addNamespaceToResultSet recursively follows namespace imports and topologically orders descriptors; remote namespace retrieval has a TODO, failures may returnfalse and addDependencies does not promote them to an explicit complete/incomplete graph receipt. No edge graph is transmitted.

The grouped namespace descriptor may have timestamp0 and empty metadata even when root result descriptor has a timestamp/project metadata. Do not reject such native-shaped duplicates merely for differing auxiliary descriptor metadata; conflicting known versions are refused.

ResourceSet.Resource.accessKey has no inspected safe-public permission meaning. The public view does not expose the field or use it as authorization. ServiceURLs remain inert data; no provider fetch or credential forwarding.

DependencyInspector/AsyncDependencyInspector inspect all native groups but always label closure UNKNOWN and edges UNAVAILABLE. Missing groups remainNone rather than asserting empty closure. Provider/version/currentness/access are server claims, not immutable source or permission leases.
Existing ResourceInspector.resolve remains its documented partial results view; historical snapshots are not silently promoted to full closure or graph acceptance.
remaining_native_obligations: Maintained complete dependency categories, edges, cross-service missingness/version/snapshot/access contracts and approved same-fixture compatibility evidence; do not substitute finite grouping for those guarantees
